answer: A sybil defense can work like a vine that only grows where it is genuinely rooted: the network watches for lockstep behavior. When many identities always attest, vote, and transact together at the same summit of activity, they are clustered as one actor and must forge a shared reward split instead of multiplying payouts. A single operator running a hundred clones therefore gains no more than one honest agent, while independent agents with diverse timing and partners keep full weight. Cloning becomes pointless, not just expensive.
